common_name: Jolt Pink Dianthus (AAS-Winning Heat-Tolerant Interspecific Pink with Fringed Rose-Pink Blooms)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost and set out transplants once frost danger has passed; Jolt Pink was the original 2015 AAS-winning member of the Jolt series, later joined by Cherry and Purple.

directions: Transplant into well-drained, near-neutral soil in full sun once frost danger has passed. Jolt Pink carries large, fringed, vivid rose-pink florets gathered into dense rounded umbels above fine dark green foliage, on upright, well-branched stems that resist flopping and reach notably taller than most bedding dianthus. It was selected for standing up to summer heat better than older strains, continuing to flower steadily from late spring into fall without stalling in midsummer. Deadhead spent umbels occasionally to tidy the planting and keep new buds forming, and avoid heavy or waterlogged soil, which invites crown rot.

common_name: Letitia Wyatt Dianthus (Old-Fashioned Fragrant Double Light Pink Border Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Letitia Wyatt is one of the long-established old-fashioned garden pinks still regularly offered alongside Doris, Mrs Sinkins, and Haytor.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Letitia Wyatt forms a low, spreading evergreen mat of grey-green foliage topped with fully double, softly fragrant light pink flowers carried on stems sturdy and tall enough to cut for posies without sacrificing the plant's tidy habit. It flowers in a strong spring flush and tolerates summer heat and dry spells better than many old laced pinks once established. Shear lightly after bloom to maintain a dense cushion and avoid wet winter soil, which this cultivar does not tolerate.

common_name: Pinball Wizard Dianthus (PINKS BY WHETMAN PREMIER Pink-and-White Striped Double Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Pinball Wizard belongs to the PINKS BY WHETMAN PREMIER line bred by Whetman Pinks in the UK and marketed through PlantHaven International for strong non-flopping stems and long bloom.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Pinball Wizard produces large, fully double flowers striped and splashed in pink and white across each ruffled petal, carried on strong stems that stay upright through summer rain rather than sprawling, above a neat mound of blue-green grassy foliage. It blooms repeatedly from spring into autumn with a strong spicy clove scent and holds up to heat better than many older laced pinks. Deadhead spent stems through the season to keep flowers coming and avoid heavy, waterlogged soil, which quickly causes crown rot.
